### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **46** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**54** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 41 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f3dbfd6c027accdd4a0e08f63050fbf0e9b575b3` — the merge of head `82b042200e8060518639c7464fc3f53bc6263ca5` into base `0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f3dbfd6c027accdd4a0e08f63050fbf0e9b575b3 && git checkout f3dbfd6c027accdd4a0e08f63050fbf0e9b575b3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4 82b042200e8060518639c7464fc3f53bc6263ca5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4 && git merge --no-ff 82b042200e8060518639c7464fc3f53bc6263ca5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review — CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER

Head-sha: `ff9ad72fbf8af10992779250472ad240a1c7e424`

**Round 1 · 2026-11-07T18:20Z**

Scope, per the narrowed rule of 2026-11-07: the spec hunks (`events`, `realtime`, `recycle-bin` with their tests, and the error-code ledger with its test), the regenerated reference pages, ADR-0148, and the code in `recycle-bin/restore.ts` that implements the refusals and the event. Also the engine wiring (the delegation stub, the operation vocabulary, `WRITE_EPOCH_OPERATIONS`) and plugin-security's fail-closed `restore`. This is an independent Fable review; the seat checked its must-fix in the code.

**Verdict: CHANGES — one must-fix and one should-fix, both local to `restore.ts`.**

Conforms (checked):
- Consent scope: the spec hunks are exactly records 6709046255 and 6710220841 (two enum members, the comment and pin flips, the fourth code, the ledger entry, the reworded doc comment). The ADR hunk is exactly the D2 bullet and one Consequences sentence.
- All-or-nothing: `judgeRestore` is read-only and runs before `writeBack`. `writeBack` runs in one transaction when every object is on the bin's driver, and compensates write by write otherwise. The entry is deleted last, and the undo is pinned.
- Events: `data.record.restored` is emitted only after the write-back commits, one per row, master first, with `after` set to the snapshot row and `organizationId` taken from the row.
- 409 is set on `status` and `httpStatus`; the ledger and `RECYCLE_BIN_RESTORE_REFUSAL_CODES` agree on four codes. `created_by` / `created_at` are kept, no insert hook runs, the D2 re-link covers both arities, and `recomputeSummaries` runs. `restore` is in the op union with `ENGINE_OPERATION_VERBS.restore = false` and is in `WRITE_EPOCH_OPERATIONS`; plugin-security denies a non-system restore with every bit set. The regenerated pages match the enums.
- The `patch` level on the spec changeset is right: AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 says `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and these are API vocabularies, not authorable keys.

**Must-fix — a parent that is in the bin as a DETAIL of another entry is refused as purged.** `parentEntryOf` (`restore.ts` ~:370–381) looks the parent up only as an entry's master (`object_name` / `record_id`). Scenario: `account a1 ← contact c1 ← task t1`, both links master-detail. Delete `t1` (entry E1 = {t1}). Delete `a1` (entry E2 = {a1, c1}). Restoring E1 then refuses `RESTORE_PARENT_PURGED`, which is permanent and says "deleted for good", even though `c1` is in E2 and restoring E2 first clears the refusal. That contradicts ADR-0148 D2 ("no longer in the bin and no longer live") and the ruling's `RESTORE_PARENT_IN_RECYCLE_BIN`. Fix: when the master lookup misses, search the caller-visible entries' `snapshot.rows` for the parent (paged, the way `emptyRecycleBin`'s fallback pages), and name the holding entry as `parentEntryId`. Add the grandchild test, with an ablation (master-only lookup ⇒ red).

**Should-fix — a transient refusal can hide a permanent one.** `judgeRestore` judges row by row (parent, then id and unique values) and throws on the first hit. Take an entry {c1, whose parent is in the bin; c2, whose id is now taken}. The caller is told to restore the parent first, does so, and only then hears `RESTORE_UNIQUE_VALUE_TAKEN`. Judge every row's permanent refusals (purged parent, id, unique values, uninstalled package) before any `RESTORE_PARENT_IN_RECYCLE_BIN`, so the first answer is the one that stands. Pin it with one test.

Nits (optional): the four code strings and the 409 are hard-coded in `restore.ts` instead of being read from `RECYCLE_BIN_RESTORE_REFUSAL_CODES` / `RECYCLE_BIN_RESTORE_REFUSAL_STATUS`, and the test pins only `parentInRecycleBin` by value. A parent whose object is unregistered falls through to IN_BIN or PURGED, and IN_BIN then names an entry that will itself refuse `PACKAGE_UNINSTALLED`. The compensating undo of a re-link goes through `engine.update`, so a failed restore publishes two `data.record.updated` for the referencing row; a comment saying so would help.

Dev questions, seat calls:
1. The ADR-0148 D5 reader table (~:298) still lists three refusal codes. That line is outside the ruling's ADR hunk, so do not edit it here. Add one `Known gap:` line to the PR body naming it; the maintainer can extend the consent by one line when merging, or it goes to a docs-only follow-up.
2. The spec changeset stays `patch` (see above).
3. The attribution link naming the card thread is acceptable.
4. The seat sets `pm:awaiting-merge` and the assignee at ACCEPT. This PR is Tier H, so a human merges it.

The patch round's delta review is Fable over `restore.ts`'s judgement only.

## Contract review — delta round 2

Head-sha: `511372165305be3e987c4a68a456ae7461ea331b`

**Delta review · 2026-11-07T19:04Z**

Scope: `restore.ts` and `restore.test.ts` since `ff9ad72fbf`. This is an independent Fable review of `judgeRestore` and `parentEntryOf`.

**Verdict: both round-1 findings are fixed. One should-fix (cost) remains before ACCEPT.**

- The must-fix is fixed. In the grandchild case (a1 ← c1 ← t1, E1 = {t1}, E2 = {a1, c1}), the master lookup misses, the keyset walk finds `c1` in E2's snapshot, and the restore refuses `RESTORE_PARENT_IN_RECYCLE_BIN` with `parentEntryId` = E2. Once E2 is restored, E1 restores. A test pins this.
- The should-fix is fixed. Every permanent refusal (an uninstalled package for all rows, a purged parent, an id or unique value taken) throws inline, and `RESTORE_PARENT_IN_RECYCLE_BIN` is answered only after the loop. The mixed-entry test pins it.
- Both bin reads take the caller's `buildDriverOptions`, so the walk stays inside the caller's organization and no other tenant's entry can be named.
- The truncated-walk path cannot be reached with production drivers: no `max` is passed, so `keysetWalk` reports `truncated` only on a reader defect.

**Should-fix — memoize the walk.** `parentEntryOf` runs once per (row, field) on the miss path, and each call walks the whole bin, parsing every entry's snapshot. Take an entry {product p1, order_line l1..l500}, where the orders went earlier as details of their customers' cascades. Restoring it walks the bin up to 500 times before it answers. Cache the result by `${object}\0${id}` within one restore, or better, collect the missing parents and resolve them all in one walk. Pin it with one test that counts the bin reads.

Nits (optional): an unregistered parent object answers `RESTORE_PARENT_PURGED`, whose sentences ("deleted for good", "nor the record of another recycle-bin entry") are then false; reword that case, or answer it as `RESTORE_PACKAGE_UNINSTALLED` naming the parent object. The truncated walk is a store defect like the unparseable-snapshot path, so a non-refusal error would be more faithful than a warning plus a permanent 409. The developer messages around `restore.ts` ~:163 and ~:189 still say "the record of another entry", and the detail-of-a-cascade case is now possible too. Skipping `entryId` in the walk is redundant but harmless.

After that patch, the seat reviews the delta in-seat and then posts ACCEPT. The PR is Tier H, so a human merges it.

## Contract review — ACCEPT

Head-sha: `82b042200e8060518639c7464fc3f53bc6263ca5`

**ACCEPT · Tier H (docs/adr) · 2026-11-07T19:47Z**

This is the in-seat delta over `511372165305` → `82b042200e`, round 3. It reads `restore.ts` and `restore.test.ts` only, per the os-dev addendum 6712176747.

- **Round 2's should-fix is resolved.** `judgeRestore` now collects every master-detail parent that is neither live nor in the entry, each one once (`missingParents`). It asks the bin about all of them through `parentEntriesOf`: one `record_id $in` read per parent object, then at most one keyset walk for the parents still unanswered, which stops once all are answered. The new pin has five details under one parent that is held as another entry's cascade row, and asserts exactly 3 bin reads. The per-reference ablation reds it, 11 ≠ 3.
- **Order of reasons.** Permanent reasons still win. The unique and id checks run in the row loop. After that, an unregistered parent object, then a parent that no entry holds, answers `RESTORE_PARENT_PURGED`. Only when no permanent reason stands does the first missing reference answer `RESTORE_PARENT_IN_RECYCLE_BIN` with its `parentEntryId`, which is ruling C. The pins and their ablations (do not judge purged first, throw on the first cause) are in the addendum.
- **Unregistered parent object.** It stays `RESTORE_PARENT_PURGED` with a sentence that names the gone object. `RESTORE_PACKAGE_UNINSTALLED` is the entry's own object, per the ledger text, so this is right.
- **Truncated walk.** It now throws a coded-less store-defect error carrying `entryId`, where before it answered purged on a reason it had not established. The seat accepts this without a pin, because a seek-ignoring full page has no honest fixture.
- **Seat nit, not owed:** a parent that is live is still probed once per referencing row (`isLive` is skipped only for a key already known missing). That costs a live read, never a bin read, and is outside the should-fix.
- **Gates:** 119 derived exit 0 with `--ran` reconciled; objectql 566 files / 11,458 tests; typecheck and eslint 0 (thread report).

Review record for the PR: round 1 Fable 6711252037 (CHANGES), round 2 Fable delta 6711739005 (one should-fix), round 3 in-seat delta (this). The ADR-0148 D5 table stays a Known gap in the PR body.

Landing: Tier H (`docs/adr/0148`), so a human merges it (os-zhuang or hotlong). It is labelled `pm:awaiting-merge` and assigned to marchtian. CI on this head was still running at ACCEPT; the human merge waits for green.
